key_points: The authors report that AWS published a guide for deploying a multimodal WhatsApp ordering assistant using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Amazon Nova 2.
The solution consolidates text, voice note, and voice call ordering into a single WhatsApp Business number with shared backend memory.
Amazon Nova 2 Lite handles text interactions while Amazon Nova 2 Sonic processes real-time speech for voice notes and calls.
The architecture uses asynchronous processing and the Model Context Protocol to separate the WhatsApp front door from backend logic.
The authors recommend enabling Amazon Bedrock Guardrails in production to ensure policy compliance and reduce hallucinations.
items.summary: The authors report that AWS has published a guide for deploying a multimodal WhatsApp ordering assistant built with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Amazon Nova 2. The solution allows quick-service restaurants to consolidate ordering across text, voice notes, and voice calls into a single WhatsApp Business number. An AI agent manages the entire order process while maintaining a unified customer history across all channels. The architecture separates the WhatsApp front door from the backend logic, using asynchronous processing to handle Meta's strict response time requirements. Deployment relies on the AWS Cloud Development Kit to provision resources like Amazon API Gateway, Lambda functions, and Amazon DynamoDB. Amazon Nova 2 Lite handles text interactions, while Amazon Nova 2 Sonic processes real-time speech for voice notes and calls. The system uses the Model Context Protocol to connect agents to backend tools without direct function calls. A single shared memory resource keyed by a hashed customer ID ensures consistent recognition regardless of the communication channel used. The authors note that costs scale primarily with conversation volume and the proportion of voice traffic. They recommend enabling Amazon Bedrock Guardrails for production environments to ensure policy compliance and reduce hallucinations.
items.title: AWS demonstrates multimodal WhatsApp ordering assistant using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

key_points: Amazon introduces a nightly workflow to systematically score, consolidate, and prune agent memories.
The solution uses three policies: TTL expiration, relevance decay scoring, and LLM-based consolidation.
A regression test suite verifies that lifecycle operations do not degrade agent response quality.
The full implementation is available as an AWS CDK stack in a public GitHub repository.
items.summary: Amazon introduces a memory lifecycle management solution for long-running agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to prevent performance degradation and compliance risks. The authors report that unmanaged memories accumulate outdated context, causing agents to reference resolved disputes or superseded advice. The solution implements three configurable policies: TTL-based expiration, relevance decay scoring, and LLM-based consolidation. A nightly workflow orchestrated by AWS Step Functions executes these policies using Lambda functions and Amazon Bedrock. The authors note that the architecture targets high-volume agents like customer support bots while allowing lower-volume agents to use simpler time-to-live settings. Testing via a regression suite ensures that pruning does not degrade response quality. The complete code is available in a GitHub repository for deployment.
items.title: Amazon introduces memory lifecycle policies for AgentCore agents

items.summary: Salman Ghouri explores the potential benefits and risks of artificial intelligence in society. The author notes that while previous technological revolutions improved productivity without causing mass unemployment, AI may be fundamentally different. Ghouri argues that unlike past inventions, AI challenges human cognition rather than just physical labor. The article highlights concerns about workers losing independent thinking skills due to over-reliance on AI tools. Ghouri mentions New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani's decision to ban generative AI in public schools as a potential response to these risks. The author concludes that humanity must learn to regulate AI responsibly rather than stopping its development entirely. Ghouri warns that uncontrolled AI advancement could lead to humans becoming dependent on machines for critical decision-making processes. The piece suggests society needs new approaches to income distribution and employment if AI significantly reduces human labor needs. Ultimately, Ghouri poses the question of whether humans will control AI or if AI will ultimately control us.
items.title: Author questions whether humanity will control AI or become controlled by it

key_points: Hydrogen cost forecasts based on experience curves are inaccurate because capacity doublings do not reflect comparable manufacturing experience.
Normalizing project costs for size reveals that apparent learning rates for electrolyzers are significantly overstated.
Growing stack sizes mean fewer physical units are produced per unit of capacity, distorting learning rate calculations.
Stacks represent only 15–20% of total capital costs, limiting the impact of manufacturing improvements on overall project prices.
Defensible forecasts must model manufacturing, scale, and system costs separately rather than using a single learning curve.
items.summary: The article argues that hydrogen cost forecasts using experience curves are flawed because they misinterpret capacity doublings. A 2025 European study shows that normalizing for project size significantly reduces apparent learning rates for electrolyzers. The author explains that larger plants share equipment rather than simply replicating units, distorting the relationship between capacity and manufacturing experience. Additionally, growing stack sizes mean fewer physical units are built for the same capacity increase, further overstating learning. The text notes that stacks comprise only 15–20% of total capital costs, limiting the impact of stack-specific improvements. The author concludes that forecasts must separate manufacturing gains from other cost drivers like electricity and logistics rather than relying on a single cumulative capacity metric.
items.title: Hydrogen cost forecasts miscount doublings due to scaling effects

items.summary: Lonely Planet has published a ranked list of the eight best castles to visit in Scotland, highlighting sites that blend royal history with rugged landscapes. The authors report that these locations range from Edinburgh Castle's volcanic rock to Dunnottar's clifftop ruins where the Scottish crown jewels were hidden. Several of these estates remain private family homes, with the Dukes of Atholl and Argyll still residing in Blair and Inveraray respectively. Access varies significantly, as sites like Dunrobin and Cawdor close entirely outside spring and summer months. Travelers must budget for long drives between distant locations such as Dunrobin in the Northern Highlands and Edinburgh in the central belt. Edinburgh Castle features the One O’Clock Gun tradition and sits atop a volcano that erupted 350 million years ago. Stirling Castle witnessed 20 sieges and was pivotal during the Wars of Scottish Independence. Eilean Donan was painstakingly reconstructed in the 20th century after being destroyed in 1719. The authors report that achieving Plan Mexico's goals requires better coordination among government institutions and increased public investment.
Mazzucato states that tax reforms targeting wealth and capital gains are necessary to fund development without burdening vulnerable populations.
The economist argues that Mexico must stop relying solely on the US market and instead build its own productive capabilities.
items.summary: Economist Mariana Mazzucato argues that Mexico must transition from being a low-cost manufacturer to developing its own technological capabilities. Speaking in an interview with EL PAÍS, she co-authored a report with Lara Merling supporting President Claudia Sheinbaum's Plan Mexico strategy. The authors report that meaningful growth requires coordinated public investment and tax reforms to address low revenues and regional disparities. Mazzucato emphasizes that the private sector must collaborate with the government to foster inclusive development rather than simply lobbying for subsidies. She also suggests restructuring the USMCA to help Mexico move up the value chain alongside Canada and the United States.
items.title: Mazzucato urges Mexico to move beyond low-cost manufacturing for US firms

key_points: A UK study of 80,000 adults found cycling and swimming linked to lower mortality while running showed no statistically significant association.
Running provides mechanical loading beneficial for bones but places excessive strain on joints compared to swimming or cycling.
Swimming reduces joint load and is ideal for those with arthritis or obesity, though it does not increase bone mineral density.
Cycling improves cardiorespiratory fitness without high joint impact but may lead to lower bone density in people who train in high volumes.
items.summary: The article explains that while running, swimming, and cycling all improve cardiovascular fitness, they produce distinct physiological responses. A UK study of 80,000 adults found that cycling and swimming were associated with lower mortality, whereas running showed no statistically significant link. Running provides mechanical loading essential for bone health but carries higher joint impact risks. Swimming reduces joint stress, making it suitable for those with pain, yet it does not build bone density. Cycling offers a middle ground for cardiorespiratory fitness but may lower bone mineral density in high-volume trainees. The authors conclude that the best choice depends on individual needs and long-term adherence rather than seeking a single superior activity.
items.title: Running, swimming, and cycling offer different health effects despite similar aerobic demands

key_points: The U.N. General Assembly voted 164 to one to back a resolution promoting world maps that show Africa's true relative size.
Togo introduced the measure on behalf of the African Group, while the United States was the only nation to vote against it.
The resolution encourages the adoption of equal-area projections like Equal Earth but does not require countries to abandon the Mercator projection.
Tom Patterson, a co-creator of the Equal Earth map, expressed surprise at the overwhelming support for the initiative.
items.summary: The United Nations General Assembly overwhelmingly adopted a resolution encouraging the use of equal-area world maps that accurately depict Africa's size. Introduced by Togo, the measure passed 164 to one, with the United States as the sole opponent. While not legally binding, the resolution urges institutions to adopt projections like Equal Earth over the traditional Mercator view. Cartographers who developed the new map expressed surprise at the vote's success.
items.title: U.N. adopts resolution to promote world maps showing Africa's true size

key_points: Football in Haiti creates social cohesion despite a security crisis that has displaced over a million people.
Criminal gangs have attacked and damaged key sports facilities, including the FIFA Goal Center and Sylvio Cator Stadium.
The Haitian U14 team won the 2025 CFU U14 Challenge Series, marking their third consecutive title.
Government officials and the Haitian Football Federation pledged continued support for youth football development.
items.summary: The article reports that football in Haiti fosters social cohesion across all classes while facing severe challenges from ongoing gang violence. Security forces and criminal groups have damaged major sports infrastructure, including the FIFA Goal Center and Sylvio Cator Stadium. Despite these obstacles, the Haitian U14 team won the 2025 CFU U14 Challenge Series, and the national team qualified for the 2026 World Cup. The Ministry of Youth, Sports, and Civic Action organized a reception for the young champions, with officials pledging continued support for youth development. Meanwhile, the U17 team prepares for the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar. The piece concludes that football remains a vital source of hope and resilience for Haitians.
items.title: Haiti football brings hope despite gang violence and security crisis

key_points: Bangladesh extended maternity leave to 120 days in April 2026, yet workers still struggle with childcare after returning.
Garment workers report that factory daycare facilities are often understaffed and inaccessible during long shifts.
The International Labour Organization notes that traditional family care systems are under pressure due to changing work patterns.
Across Bangladesh, Vietnam, and Cambodia, women sustain garment production while families absorb much of the necessary childcare.
Workers describe exhaustion and production targets that prevent them from using available breastfeeding and childcare facilities.
items.summary: Bangladesh's Parliament amended labour laws in April 2026 to extend maternity benefits from 112 to 120 days for eligible workers. Despite this legal improvement, garment workers like Morsheda and Mina report that childcare remains a critical barrier after their leave ends. Workers often rely on grandparents or paid caregivers because factory daycare facilities are understaffed and inaccessible during long shifts. The International Labour Organization notes that traditional family care systems are under pressure as work patterns change. While international brands highlight policies as progress, workers describe exhaustion and production targets that prevent them from using available facilities. Across Bangladesh, Vietnam, and Cambodia, women sustain garment production while families absorb much of the necessary childcare.
items.title: Bangladesh extends maternity leave but garment workers lack childcare

items.title: Owaisi and Yadav question UP government over early mosque demolition

key_points: Overseas investors remained net buyers across Indian sectors during the second half of August.
Consumer Services attracted the highest inflows at Rs 5,019 crore during the fortnight.
Telecom and Power sectors faced continued selling pressure with significant capital outflows.
SBI Securities linked consumer sector growth to higher disposable income and aspirational spending.
items.summary: Overseas investors remained net buyers across Indian sectors during the second half of August, marking two consecutive fortnights of inflows. The National Securities Depository reported that ten sectors recorded Foreign Portfolio Investor activity between August 16 and August 31. Consumer Services attracted the highest inflows at Rs 5,019 crore, while Financial Services received over Rs 4,000 crore. SBI Securities attributed this interest to rising disposable income and a shift toward aspirational spending. Conversely, Telecom and Power sectors faced continued selling pressure, with FPIs withdrawing Rs 4,983 crore and Rs 2,641 crore respectively. Analysts noted that infrastructure costs and cash flow constraints continue to weigh on these industries.
items.title: Foreign investors poured $3 billion into Indian markets in late August

The growth is driven by demand for AI servers and data centers.
Analysts expected a 37% sales increase for the quarter ending September.
Hon Hai continues to face modest margins from its Apple smartphone business.

key_points: The banking system liquidity surplus reached a record ₹10.3 trillion, surpassing the previous high of ₹9.7 trillion.
The RBI conducted a ₹7 trillion variable rate reverse repo auction to manage the excess liquidity before the October policy review.
India's foreign exchange reserves rose to $740.8 billion, primarily supported by foreign currency assets increasing by nearly $60 billion over nine weeks.
Market participants believe the central bank may avoid additional liquidity-tightening measures before the upcoming monetary policy meeting.
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India faces a record liquidity surplus of ₹10.3 trillion, increasing the likelihood of an interest rate hike at its October meeting. A ₹7 trillion variable rate reverse repo auction aims to absorb excess funds driven by foreign currency inflows. While foreign exchange reserves climbed to $740.8 billion, market participants note the central bank must now balance growth support with inflation risks and market stability.
items.title: RBI Liquidity Surplus Hits Record as Rate Hike Chances Rise

key_points: People familiar with the matter say Anthropic will likely begin marketing its IPO in mid-October.
The company is expected to file its prospectus in late September instead of next week.
Analysts anticipate a $15 billion revolving credit facility as part of the financing process.
Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, and Citi are working with Anthropic on the offering.

The company aims to complete the listing before the U.S. midterm elections in November. Analysts expect the deal to involve a $15 billion revolving credit facility. Major banks including Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs are assisting with the process. Anthropic declined to comment on the reported timeline changes.
items.title: Anthropic delays IPO launch to mid-October amid election timing

key_points: Tata Motors launched a voluntary tender offer for all Iveco Group common shares at €14.1 each.
The acceptance period runs from September 7, 2026, to October 26, 2026.
Exor N.V. has irrevocably committed to support the offer and tender its 27.06% shareholding.
The combined entity will have annual sales of approximately 590,000 units and revenues of €21 billion.
items.summary: Tata Motors Ltd announced a voluntary tender offer for all common shares of Iveco Group N.V. at €14.1 per share. The offer, made by Tata Motors step-down subsidiary TML CV Holdings B.V., runs from September 7 to October 26, 2026. Exor N.V. has committed to tendering approximately 27.06% of common shares. The transaction values Iveco Group at roughly €3.82 billion and requires a 95% acceptance level. Both companies' CEOs stated the merger creates a stronger global commercial vehicle business with over 590,000 annual sales. Combined revenues reach €21 billion across Europe, India, South America, and the rest of the world. All necessary regulatory clearances have been obtained, and the deal aims for 100% acquisition and delisting from the Milan stock exchange.
items.title: Tata Motors launches tender offer for Iveco Group shares at €14.1 each

key_points: RBI forex reserves reached a record $740.80 billion for the week ended August 28.
The central bank's special swap window contributed $136.3 billion in cumulative inflows since June.
Senior economist Radhika Rao observed a shift in intervention bias due to strong FCNR inflows.
The RBI absorbed over ₹6.02 lakh crore from the banking system through variable rate reverse repo auctions.
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India reported that forex reserves hit a new high of $740.80 billion for the week ended August 28. This increase of $11.475 billion surpasses the previous record set in February. The central bank attributes the rise to its special swap window, which has raised cumulative inflows of $136.3 billion since June. Senior economist Radhika Rao noted a shift in intervention bias as strong FCNR inflows helped stabilize the rupee. Additionally, the RBI absorbed over ₹6.02 lakh crore from the banking system through variable rate reverse repo auctions.
items.title: RBI Forex Reserves Reach Record $740.80 Billion Due to Special Swap Measures

items.title: US envoy Sergio Gor hints at India-US trade deal finalization in next few months

India and Belgium signed a Letter of Intent on Defence Cooperation and a memorandum of understanding between their defence industries.

items.title: CBI files FIR against Subhash Chandra over alleged net worth inflation for loans

Built in 1878 by William Nelson Chancellor, the 5,827-square-foot mansion features 64 windows and a river-view tower.
Realtor.com and the current property listing confirm the sale details and historical context.
The home retains historic elements like gas chandeliers while featuring a modern kitchen and updated bathroom.
items.summary: The Chancellor House in Parkersburg, West Virginia, is listed for $695,000 after remaining in the same family for 148 years. Built in 1878 by William Nelson Chancellor, the 5,827-square-foot Second Empire-style home has housed five generations of the Chancellor family. Realtor.com and the current property listing confirm the sale details. The property features 64 windows, walnut woodwork, and a tower overlooking the Ohio River. Catherine Brown, a fifth-generation descendant, lived there most of her life before the sale.
items.title: 148-year-old West Virginia mansion stays in one family, now listed for sale

items.title: Delhi Police arrest Swatantra Bhardwaj and send him to one-day custody

items.title: Dutch NGO offers job to Indian youth who cleaned polluted river

The Nepal Army, working with South Korean disaster response specialists, pulled a Chinese national alive from a 225-metre tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project.

Specific areas in Delhi and NCR are likely to experience rainfall accompanied by lightning over the next two hours.
Heavy rains on Friday disrupted flight operations at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport.
Fresh showers on Saturday morning caused traffic disruptions in Gurugram.

Heavy downpours on Friday disrupted flight operations at Indira Gandhi International Airport, while fresh showers on Saturday morning impacted traffic in Gurugram. Kotak believes splitting ITC into separate entities could unlock significant shareholder value by attracting different investor pools. The firm notes that current valuations may reflect stagnant earnings expectations or limited appetite for the tobacco sector.
items.title: Kotak Securities suggests ITC tobacco business is undervalued by the market

key_points: Torrential rain left several parts of Delhi waterlogged, affecting key areas and roads.
MCD Chairman Satya Sharma said municipal staff are working relentlessly to clear water upon receiving complaints.
MCD Mayor Pravesh Wahi noted the situation is less severe than before and highlighted the deployment of two specialized suction vehicles.

items.summary: Heavy rain caused severe waterlogging across Delhi, disrupting traffic and airport routes. MCD officials stated that teams are working to clear water and claimed the situation is better than previous instances. The corporation deployed two high-capacity suction vehicles to manage flooding. While the IMD issued red alerts and recorded high rainfall at Palam, airlines warned passengers of possible delays due to adverse weather conditions.
items.title: Delhi waterlogging affects roads and airport; MCD officials defend drainage response

items.title: Sheikh Hasina plans December return to Bangladesh amid political uncertainty

Approximately 10.26 lakh people in 11 districts have been affected by the floods.
The state government has deployed 858 boats and multiple relief teams for evacuation and rescue operations.
The Water Resources Department forecasts the Ganga water level at Gandhi Ghat could rise to 50.62 metres by Sunday morning.
items.summary: The Ganga river breached its highest flood mark in Patna as severe rains impacted 11 districts in Bihar. items.title: Chennai police reopen POCSO case against mining baron after court intervention
